BLOCKED (batch_096, 2026-09-08) -- RIGHTS: the rights holder's own page states a PERMISSION-REQUIRED condition on use of the ZTPI, so no mavromoustakos_2016_ztpi__items.csv was written. THE CLAUSE, quoted verbatim from Philip Zimbardo's own first-person Social Psychology Network profile (http://zimbardo.socialpsychology.org/overview, fetched 2026-09-08): "The Zimbardo Time Perspective Inventory (ZTPI). It is presented, along with scoring rules, on the web site. Researchers can use it free with my permission and agreement to share results." The same page adds a control on derivatives: "Before starting a translation, please contact my French colleague who can inform you of existing scales in each language: Dr.Nicolas Fieulaine of Lyon". Under SKILL.md's 'Rights on the wording' test (superseding 2026-09-05, irw#1945) this RESERVES A RIGHT rather than disclaiming fitness: permission-required is the first-listed block trigger, and 'free to researchers, conditioned on my permission and on an agreement to share results' is the free-but-restricted shape already ruled on for HEXACO, TIMSS and PROMIS. IRW redistributes: hosting the 56 statements hands them to downstream users who have neither sought Zimbardo's permission nor agreed to share results, which is exactly the use the clause conditions, so 'our own use would comply' is not a defence. WHY THE SWLS TWO-PAGES RULING DOES NOT RESCUE IT. The obvious counter-argument is the 2026-09-04 SWLS ruling (the terms of the page you actually took the wording from govern, even between two pages of one rights holder). The full 56-item instrument is distributed as a PDF at http://zimbardo.socialpsychology.org/file/ZTPI.pdf (sha256 87109dc4f2af257df0a16d63fecd955e1f80f86bd8eedd24823911ac7be57e41, 6pp, fetched 2026-09-08), and that PDF carries NO copyright, permission, reproduction or distribution notice anywhere in its text (grepped for copyright|permission|reproduc|distribut|licen|all rights: zero hits). But that PDF is hosted BY the very profile page that carries the clause -- it is listed on zimbardo.socialpsychology.org as 'Other Files: Zimbardo Time Perspective Inventory / ZTPI.pdf (82.5KB)' -- so this is one page stating terms and distributing the document, not two pages with different terms. There is no more-permissive sibling page to prefer. (philipzimbardo.com/research/time-perspective carries the same sentence rewritten into the third person with 'my permission' dropped -- "Researchers can use it free with agreement to share results" -- which is a memorial rewrite of the same statement, still a stated use restriction, and in any case not the page the PDF sits on. sha256 of that page as fetched 07866535d95155d28a8b1a2fbbe019d4d333305e593d20aa7a7bd9cd48c535eb; note both socialpsychology.org and philipzimbardo.com pages carry a rotating news sidebar so their whole-page hashes drift -- the ZTPI.pdf hash above is the stable artefact.) WHAT THE TABLE IS (Step 3b, checked before the rights question was reached, and clean). The live item set is ZTPIQ1..ZTPIQ56 with an R suffix on exactly 9, 24, 25 and 41, and resp is 1-5. That is the ORIGINAL 56-item Zimbardo & Boyd (1999) ZTPI, not one of the 15-/17-item short forms: the item count is 56 and the four R-marked codes are precisely the ZTPI's four canonical reverse-scored items (9, 24, 25, 41), which no short form reproduces. The paper's Methods say only the Past-Negative, Present-Hedonistic and Future subscales were ANALYSED, but the deposit .sav holds all 56 administered columns, so the table is the whole instrument. SOURCES CHECKED BEFORE THE BLOCK. (a) The study's own S1 File .sav (PLOS 10.1371/journal.pone.0161272.s001, cached) -- pyreadstat over all 56 ZTPIQ columns returns column_names_to_labels = None for every one, and the file's only value-label sets are group ('Non-flying phobic'/'Flying phobic') and 'low'/'high'; the level-1 source carries no item text at either level, so data_labels was never available. (b) The PLOS ONE article itself (CC BY 4.0) reproduces exactly one ZTPI statement in passing ('Painful past experiences keep being replayed in my mind.') and no item list. So the only route to wording was the canonical instrument, i.e. Zimbardo's own distribution -- which is the restricted source. Per the 2026-09-08 ruling that a CC BY appendix does not launder a restricted instrument, the PLOS deposit's licence governs the response data only and does not reach the wording. DOES THE BLOCK ACHIEVE ANYTHING? Yes. Unlike the irw#2101/#2123 case, the IRW item codes here are opaque ('ZTPIQ37'), carrying only the instrument name and an item number, so withholding item text genuinely withholds the wording; the response table leaks none of it. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. This is not an access failure: every source was retrieved successfully (the .sav, the article, the ZTPI PDF and both rights pages, all HTTP 200 and cached), the instrument was positively identified, and a verdict was reached. An unchanged retry today reproduces this exact result. What would have to change: either Zimbardo's estate/rights holder replaces the permission-required condition with an unconditional grant, or Ben rules that a grant conditioned on 'my permission and agreement to share results' is not a reserved right for IRW's purposes. WORTH ESCALATING rather than filing away, because the ZTPI is a recurring instrument in the corpus and this is the first table to reach the question: a ruling would settle every future ZTPI table at once, and the register (itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv) currently holds no ZTPI row -- one should be added by the orchestrator (instrument='Zimbardo Time Perspective Inventory (ZTPI)', family='ZTPI', verdict='block', rule='permission_required', clause and source_url as quoted above).
